# Build a Simple Siri Shortcut to Create a Weekly Grocery List with Apple Intelligence

By the end of this guide you'll have a shortcut on your iPhone that asks what you're cooking this week, hands your answer to Apple Intelligence, and gives you back a grocery list. A **shortcut** is a small set of steps the Shortcuts app runs for you in order; Apple calls each step an **action**. Once it's saved, you start it by asking Siri for it by name.

## Before you start
- An iPhone that supports Apple Intelligence, with Apple Intelligence turned on and the latest iOS installed. Apple keeps the list of supported models on its website, and notes that Apple Intelligence isn't available in all languages or regions and that usage limits may apply.
- The **Shortcuts** app — it comes with the iPhone; if you deleted it, it's free in the App Store.
- About **10 minutes**.

The button and action names below come from Apple's Shortcuts User Guide. If your iPhone is set to another language, you'll see them translated.

## Step 1 — Create a new shortcut and name it
Open the **Shortcuts** app and tap the **Add** button (the plus sign). A new, empty shortcut opens. Tap **New Shortcut** at the top, tap **Rename**, type **Weekly Grocery List**, and confirm. The name matters: it's exactly what you'll say to Siri later, so keep it short and easy to say.
You'll know it worked when the new name appears at the top of the empty shortcut.

💬 Example: name it `Weekly Grocery List`.

## Step 2 — Ask yourself what you're cooking
Tap **Add Action**, search for **Ask for Input**, and tap it to add it. Apple describes this action like this: when the shortcut runs, it opens a box that asks a question, and when you answer and tap **Done**, your answer is passed to the next action. Tap the question text inside the action and type your own question. Leave the answer type as text, because you'll type a few meal names.
You'll know it worked when the action shows your question.

💬 Example: type `What are you cooking this week?` as the question.

## Step 3 — Let Apple Intelligence write the list
Swipe up on the search field at the bottom of the screen, search for **Use Model**, and tap it. Choose **On-Device** — Apple says it handles simple requests without needing a network connection. (For a long, complicated week you can pick **Cloud**, which uses Apple's Private Cloud Compute.) In the text field below **Use Model**, type your prompt. Apple's guide says the prompt can include the output of a previous action: type the prompt below, then, at the very end, pick the answer from Step 2 from the suggestions above the keyboard (Shortcuts usually calls it **Provided Input**).
You'll know it worked when the Use Model action shows your prompt with the answer from Step 2 inside it.

💬 Example: "Make a grocery list for the meals below. Group the items by store section, one item per line, and skip basic spices. Meals:"

## Step 4 — Turn on Follow Up so you can fix the list
Tap the arrow next to **Use Model**, then tap the **Follow Up** checkbox. Apple's guide describes this as a way to keep talking to the model and refine its answer before the shortcut moves on. That's useful here: you can say "I already have rice and eggs, take them off" without starting again.
You'll know it worked when the Follow Up checkbox is ticked.

## Step 5 — Run it with Siri
Tap **Done** to save. Now activate Siri and say the name of your shortcut — Apple's guide: activate Siri, then say the name of a shortcut. Siri asks your question from Step 2; answer with your meals, for example "tacos, lentil soup and a roast chicken". A moment later the grocery list appears, and you can ask for changes. When it's right, copy it into Notes or Reminders.
You'll know it worked when a grocery list based on your meals appears on screen.

💬 Example: say `Hey Siri, Weekly Grocery List`, then answer `tacos, lentil soup and a roast chicken`.

## Common mistakes
- **You can't find Use Model:** Apple Intelligence may be turned off, your iPhone may not support it, or it may not be available in your language or region yet. The rest of the shortcut still works without it.
- **Naming the shortcut like a normal Siri request:** Apple warns that if a shortcut has the same name as a standard Siri command, Siri runs the shortcut instead. Pick a name like "Weekly Grocery List", not "What's the weather".
- **Trusting the list blindly:** the model doesn't know what's already in your fridge, and it can forget an item. Read the list once before you go shopping.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** Planning the week's shopping becomes a 30-second voice chat instead of a scrap of paper you forget at home.
- **For your business or work:** The same pattern — a question, then Use Model — works for packing lists for a work trip or supplies for a team event.
- **If you're just getting started:** Build only Steps 1–3 first and run the shortcut from the app. Add Follow Up and Siri once that works.

## Try it now
Open Shortcuts, tap **Add**, name the shortcut **Weekly Grocery List**, add **Ask for Input** and **Use Model** with the prompt above, and tap **Done**. Then say "Hey Siri, Weekly Grocery List" — your first list is about five minutes away.
